claims.claim: When an abnormal price move appears, seek company disclosures, news, volume, and peer or sector moves before treating it as durable repricing; act on the catalyst review the same day, and reject the repricing interpretation if no incremental information or abnormal trading activity exists. Likewise, treat unusually high short interest as nondirectional positioning risk: verify float percentage, days to cover, borrow cost, utilization, liquidity, and catalysts over days to weeks, with falling short interest without price pressure or disproof of the bearish concerns as falsifiers.
claims.why: The shown observations consistently make conspicuous market data a research trigger rather than a directional conclusion and attach evidence requirements, action horizons, and explicit falsifiers.
uncertainty_notes: The denominator and days-to-cover measure are not shown.
contradiction_notes: High short interest alone does not establish either a squeeze or a short case.

claims.claim: When a downstream bottleneck or labor shift is linked to an investment beneficiary, validate every causal hop before acting: for a supply chain, test material intensity, supplier share, inventories, qualification cycles, alternatives, and whether the proposed input is actually binding during the demand ramp; for automation, distinguish structural substitution from cyclical weakness using employment, implementation, productivity, wage, and margin evidence over multiple years. Abandon the respective inference if another component is the real constraint, or if cyclical explanations dominate, automation is not implemented, or margin expansion fails to appear.
claims.why: Both shown causal-hop units require evidence that the proposed intermediary mechanism is binding rather than accepting a plausible thematic narrative as causation.
uncertainty_notes: The assertion that one small supplier bottlenecks the entire buildout is unverified.
The attribution of the payroll revision to AI is asserted without causal evidence.

claims.claim: When an enabling component or new platform suggests cross-sector or multi-tier supplier exposure, trace supplier-to-customer relationships, compatibility, qualification, vendor share, bill-of-materials content, adoption commitments, substitutability, and end-market demand before assigning optionality or initiating exposure. Over the medium term to two years, prefer links where platform volume has the clearest and least commoditized revenue connection; falsify the mapping if qualification is absent, adoption stalls, vendor share changes, or substitution occurs.
claims.why: The shown identity-provenance units make verified commercial identity and revenue linkage prerequisites for translating thematic overlap into investable exposure.
uncertainty_notes: The central supplier mapping is explicitly described as highly possible rather than confirmed.
Several supplier relationships are explicitly speculative.

claims.claim: When a company appears to trade below the value of a separately valued stake, calculate adjusted net asset value using ownership, realizability, liabilities, tax leakage, governance constraints, and operating-business economics, then monitor credible monetization, sale, or listing catalysts. Infer asymmetric value only conditionally; reject it if the stake is illiquid, encumbered, overvalued, or unmonetizable, or if the operating business deteriorates.
claims.why: The shown value-capture unit distinguishes quoted stake value from realizable parent-level value and ties action to a concrete recognition mechanism.
uncertainty_notes: The text does not establish net debt, tax leakage, governance constraints, or the realizable value of the stake.

claims.claim: When an option chain displays breakevens far above the underlying price, interpret the displayed upside primarily as a premium hurdle rather than a probability-weighted forecast. Before entry and throughout the holding period, compare premiums, open interest, liquidity, implied volatility, strikes, and expiries, and select only liquid contracts whose expiry accommodates the catalyst window; falsify the claim of an unusually demanding hurdle if a liquid chain offers modest premiums and thesis-consistent breakevens.
claims.why: The same shown unit is canonically coded on both value capture and timing, supporting an interface that joins required underlying movement, contract pricing, liquidity, and thesis duration.
uncertainty_notes: The screenshot does not show premiums, volume, or open interest for each contract.

claims.claim: When policy restricts a competitor or a contract appears to rerate a supplier, test whether the apparent catalyst can convert into usable economics. For a supply restriction, verify its scope, displaced capacity, substitutes, customer qualification, and the beneficiary's usable capacity immediately after implementation; the pricing-power inference fails if competitors retain access or customers qualify alternatives. For a contract, validate value, duration, revenue recognition, margins, financing needs, execution capacity, valuation, and price reaction over months to years before treating backlog as captured value.
claims.why: The shown catalyst units require both demand transfer and operational or financial conversion, preventing a headline event from being equated with realized value.
uncertainty_notes: The post does not substantiate the claimed monopoly.

claims.claim: When external financing or public support accompanies expansion, evaluate the full conversion from capital to per-share operating value. For an active at-the-market program, track remaining capacity, share count, use of proceeds, and completion, deferring exposure while dilution impairs per-share value unless the funded activity produces greater accretion. For conditional public funding, monitor award finalization, conditions, capex timing, usable capacity, and customer demand over the medium to long term; reject the catalyst if funding is withdrawn or reduced, or fails to create incremental usable capacity.
claims.why: The shown capital-structure units separate gross enterprise expansion from per-share accretion and completed operating capacity.
uncertainty_notes: The stated program size and peer comparison are unverified.

claims.claim: When a company raises capital after securing contracted growth, do not classify dilution as automatically destructive or beneficial. Compare dilution size and price, contract duration and economics, use of proceeds, execution funding, and post-raise valuation over the contract horizon; infer accretion only if proceeds fund value creation exceeding ownership dilution, and falsify that inference if funds are not deployed to execution, expected revenue fails, or dilution exceeds the value created.
claims.why: The shown contradiction unit resolves a financing event through its use of proceeds and per-share value creation rather than through the financing label alone.
uncertainty_notes: The claim that dilution was already priced in requires market evidence.
contradiction_notes: Dilution harms existing ownership but may support higher-value growth if proceeds are productively deployed.

claims.claim: When price falls sharply without an identified fundamental change—or rises while a bottleneck thesis remains outstanding—reassess contracts, recurring revenue, demand, customer conversion, qualification, scalable capacity, valuation, multi-sourcing, and adoption milestones rather than using the price move itself as the verdict. Maintain or reassess over the thesis horizon only while those fundamentals remain intact; falsify the thesis on material demand or revenue deterioration, failed qualification, lost sourcing position, inability to scale, or failure of the relevant architecture to ramp.
claims.why: The shown bear-falsifier units define thesis failure through operating and commercialization evidence rather than recent price direction.
uncertainty_notes: Institutional-accumulation explanation is asserted rather than demonstrated.
The supplier claims, customer relationships, and long-term valuation case are not independently verified.
contradiction_notes: The post says the name is widely undiscovered despite noting a gain of more than 50%.

claims.claim: When a single anecdote or unconfirmed report suggests scarce capacity, use it only to trigger corroboration: seek provider waitlists, utilization, reservation contracts, pricing, and comparable customer reports in the near term. Infer market scarcity only after provider-level confirmation, and reject it if capacity is broadly available or the report proves to be an isolated account issue.
claims.why: The shown confidence-hedge unit explicitly distinguishes an early research lead from sufficient market-wide evidence.
uncertainty_notes: The evidence is anecdotal and does not establish market-wide availability.

claims.claim: When subsequent outcomes become observable, evaluate the method with a complete time-stamped ledger containing entries, exits, open positions, losses, benchmarks, and attribution to the originally stated catalysts, option flows, earnings, and macro signals. Test for persistent value rather than highlighting isolated wins; falsify the claimed edge if the complete benchmarked record shows none.
claims.why: The shown postmortem unit defines process quality through complete, time-stamped, benchmarked outcome attribution.
uncertainty_notes: The list is self-selected and lacks exits, benchmarks, and a complete loss record.

claims.claim: When a thesis suffers an immediate event-driven drawdown, distinguish a timing error from thesis failure by checking whether the required operating milestones remain intact over the originally stated duration. Reassess milestones and horizon over months or longer rather than extrapolating the drawdown; classify the thesis as failed when the required milestones fail, not merely when they are delayed.

shown_code_refs.label: Separate timing error from thesis failure

claims.why: The shown postmortem unit explicitly separates short-horizon forecast error from evidence about a longer-duration operating thesis.
uncertainty_notes: The later performance example does not prove the current thesis will recover.
contradiction_notes: The author concedes being wrong on the short-term time frame.
